previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of NSTEMI and ventricular tachycardia was admitted after an asymptomatic episode of sustained monomorphic VT during dialysis. She was treated with IV amiodarone and magnesium, converted to sinus rhythm, and started on oral amiodarone and mexiletine with close QTc monitoring. Her QTc peaked at 530 ms but improved to 460 ms by discharge. She had melena on admission due to bleeding gastric polyps, with hemoglobin declining from 10.3 to 7.8 g/dL, but it stabilized without transfusion. Pain from calciphylaxis was managed with increased fentanyl patch and Dilaudid; IV thiosulfate was deferred due to arrhythmia risk. She received dialysis and a fistulogram during admission, was evaluated by dermatology, wound care, and palliative care, and was discharged to extended care with plans for wound management, medication adherence, and follow-up.

INDICATION:  History: ___ with prior VT, 3d/wk dialysis  // ?cpd

TECHNIQUE:  AP portable radiograph

COMPARISON:  Radiograph dated ___

FINDINGS: 

AP portable semi upright chest radiograph demonstrates cardiomegaly.  Dense
coronary artery calcifications are better appreciated on prior study.  There
is no evidence of pulmonary edema.  Lungs are otherwise clear without a focal
opacity.  There is no pneumothorax.  There is no pleural effusion.  No air
under the right hemidiaphragm is seen.  A clip is noted in the right upper
quadrant.  Suture material is seen at the right apex.

IMPRESSION: 

Cardiomegaly without overt pulmonary edema.

EXAMINATION:  CTA ABD AND PELVIS

INDICATION:  History: ___ with prior episodes ischemia, elevated lactate,
guaiac pos  // ?mesenteric ischemia

TECHNIQUE:  Abdomen and pelvis CTA: Non-contrast and aortic phase
post-contrast images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis.
Oral contrast was not administered.
MIP reconstructions were performed on independent workstation and reviewed on
PACS.

DOSE:  Acquisition sequence:
   1) Spiral Acquisition 4.2 s, 46.0 cm; CTDIvol = 2.1 mGy (Body) DLP = 97.0
mGy-cm.
   2) Spiral Acquisition 6.0 s, 46.9 cm; CTDIvol = 7.1 mGy (Body) DLP = 331.1
mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Body) = 428 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis dated ___

FINDINGS: 

VASCULAR:

There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is severe calcium burden in the
abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.  Apparent filling defects are
seen, narrowing the branches of the abdominal aorta, though it appears chronic
in nature.

LOWER CHEST: There is bibasilar atelectasis.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. There
is no evidence of focal lesions. There is no evidence of intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is is resected.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation. There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are atrophic with extensive vascular calcifications and
scattered calculi.  Hypodense lesions in the bilateral kidneys likely
represent cysts.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is distended with ingested material.  There is
mucosal enhancement, which is prominent, and is of unclear significance. 
Bowel loops are collapsed and demonstrate normal wall thickness.  Though the
distal small bowel enhances somewhat less briskly than the proximal small
bowel, there are no secondary signs of ischemia, such as bowel wall thickening
or adjacent fluid.  Dense contrast material is seen within the lumen of the
left hemicolon, extending into the sigmoid and the rectum, and somewhat
obscures this examination.  The patient is status post partial colectomy with
an and ileocolonic anastomosis.

RETROPERITONEUM: Multiple, enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes are seen in
the pericaval, aortocaval, and para-aortic regions.  A prominent caps
pericaval node measuring 1 cm in short axis (3:79) is noted.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  There is no
evidence of pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  Small free fluid may be
present, though evaluation is obscured due to a right hip arthroplasty.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus is not visualized.

BONES: Multilevel degenerative changes are noted, including anterolisthesis of
L4 on L5, on a degenerative basis.  There is evidence of renal osteodystrophy.

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:


1. Extensive vascular calcification narrowing the lumen of the abdominal
arteries.  The distal small bowel does not enhance as briskly as the more
proximal small bowel.  There are no definite secondary signs of bowel
ischemia. Examination is somewhat obscured by dense contrast material in the
colon.
2. Retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy similar to prior.

EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST Q111 CT HEAD.

material performed during the CT of the abdomen and pelvis on ___
at 23:16 hr.  Within this limitation, grossly there is no evidence of

calcification as well as cerebellar calcifications related with known history

hemorrhage, edema, or mass.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and

There is no evidence of fracture.  Lucencies within the mandibular condyles

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___,
performed the procedure.
ANESTHESIA:  1% lidocaine
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  0.9 min, 2 mGy

PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks,
benefits and alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was
obtained from the patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography
suite and placed supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was
performed per ___ protocol.  The right neck was prepped and draped in the
usual sterile fashion.
Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent right internal jugular vein
was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent
ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which
confirmed vein patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right
atrium using fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath.
The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was advanced into the IVC.
A triple-lumen central venous catheter was advanced over the wire into the
superior vena cava with the tip in the cavoatrial junction. All 3 access ports
were aspirated, flushed and capped. The catheter was secured to the skin with
a 0 silk suture and sterile dressings were applied. Final spot fluoroscopic
image demonstrating good alignment of the catheter and no kinking. The patient
tolerated the procedure well without immediate complications.

FINDINGS: 

Patent right internal jugular vein. Final fluoroscopic image showing triple
lumen central venous catheter with catheter tip terminating in the distal
superior vena cava.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a temporary triple lumen catheter via the right
internal jugular venous approach. The tip of the catheter terminates in the
distal superior vena cava. The catheter is ready for use.

2. Unchanged moderate right and trace left pleural effusions.  Minimally
improved bibasilar atelectasis.
3. Stable moderate-to-severe cardiomegaly.
